prompt.adult: How old was David when he began to reign as king?
prompt.child: David became king. How old was he when he started?
prompt.teen: At what age did David begin his reign?
prompt.older: According to 2 Samuel 5:4, how old was David when he began to reign?

verses.text: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.

explanation.adult: 2 Samuel 5:4 gives David's age at the start of his reign, then how long he reigned.
explanation.child: Read the first part of 2 Samuel 5:4.
explanation.teen: 2 Samuel 5:4 has two numbers. The first is his age when he began.
explanation.older: 2 Samuel 5:4 summarizes David's reign: age at accession, then total length.

teaching.extended_explanation: 2 Samuel 5:4 gives two facts about David's reign. Read the first one again.
teaching.takeaway: David was thirty years old when he began to reign.

prompt.adult: Where did the elders of Israel come to anoint David king over Israel?
prompt.child: All the leaders of Israel came to make David their king. Where did they go?
prompt.teen: In which town did King David make a covenant with Israel's elders and get anointed king over Israel?
prompt.older: According to 2 Samuel 5:3, where was David anointed king over Israel?

verses.text: Therefore all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and King David made a covenant with them at Hebron before the LORD. And they anointed David king over Israel.

explanation.adult: 2 Samuel 5:3 names the place twice in its first sentence.
explanation.child: Read 2 Samuel 5:3. Look for where the elders came to the king.
explanation.teen: 2 Samuel 5:3 says where the elders came and where the covenant was made. It is the same place.
explanation.older: 2 Samuel 5:3 repeats the place name to stress the covenant setting before the anointing.

teaching.extended_explanation: All the elders of Israel came to David in one place. Read 2 Samuel 5:3 again to find it.
teaching.takeaway: The elders of Israel anointed David king over Israel at Hebron.

review.notes: Rooted stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _rooted_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: When the ark was brought up, what did David do before the LORD with all his might?
prompt.child: David was full of joy as the ark of God came. What did he do with all his might?
prompt.teen: Wearing a linen ephod, how did David celebrate before the LORD as the ark came?
prompt.older: According to 2 Samuel 6:14, what did David do before the LORD with all his might?

verses.text: Then David danced before the LORD with all his might; and David was wearing a linen ephod.

explanation.adult: 2 Samuel 6:14 tells what David did and how. Read the first part of the verse.
explanation.teen: 2 Samuel 6:14 says David did something "before the LORD with all his might." Find the action.
explanation.older: 2 Samuel 6:14 describes David's worship and his clothing; the verb comes right after his name.

teaching.extended_explanation: David was full of joy as the ark came to the City of David. Read 2 Samuel 6:14 to see how he showed it.
teaching.takeaway: David danced before the LORD with all his might.

review.notes: Rooted stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _rooted_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: David first reigned over Judah for seven years and six months. After that, from which city did he reign over all Israel and Judah?
prompt.child: For seven and a half years David ruled only Judah. Then he ruled all of Israel and Judah from a new city. Which one?
prompt.teen: After his first seven and a half years as king of Judah, where did David reign over the whole nation?
prompt.older: According to 2 Samuel 5:5, from which city did David reign over all Israel and Judah?

verses.text: In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.

explanation.adult: 2 Samuel 5:5 names two cities. The second one is where he reigned over all Israel and Judah.
explanation.child: Read the second half of 2 Samuel 5:5.
explanation.teen: 2 Samuel 5:5 splits David's reign into two parts. Look at the second part.
explanation.older: 2 Samuel 5:5 divides the reign into two periods by city; the longer period answers the question.

teaching.extended_explanation: David's reign had two parts in two places. 2 Samuel 5:5 names the city for the second part. Read it again.
teaching.takeaway: David reigned over all Israel and Judah from Jerusalem.

prompt.adult: David lived in a cedar palace. Where did he say the ark of God was dwelling?
prompt.child: David told Nathan he had a fine cedar home. Where was the ark of God staying?
prompt.teen: Why was David bothered while living in his cedar palace? Where was the ark of God dwelling?
prompt.older: According to 2 Samuel 7:2, where was the ark of God dwelling?

choices.text: Under an oak tree near the city

verses.text: that the king said to Nathan the prophet, “See now, I dwell in a house of cedar, but the ark of God dwells inside tent curtains.”

explanation.adult: 2 Samuel 7:2 contrasts where David lived with where the ark was. Read the end of the verse.
explanation.child: Read the last part of 2 Samuel 7:2.
explanation.teen: In 2 Samuel 7:2, David compares two dwellings. Find the one for the ark.
explanation.older: 2 Samuel 7:2 sets David's comfort against the ark's humbler dwelling; the second clause gives it.

teaching.extended_explanation: David noticed a difference between his home and the ark's. Read the end of 2 Samuel 7:2.
teaching.takeaway: The ark of God dwelt inside tent curtains while David lived in cedar.

prompt.adult: Through Nathan, the LORD told David how long his throne would be established. How long?
prompt.child: God sent Nathan with a promise about David's throne. How long would it last?
prompt.teen: The LORD's promise to David through Nathan said his kingdom and throne would be established for how long?
prompt.older: According to 2 Samuel 7:16, for how long would David's throne be established?

verses.text: And your house and your kingdom shall be established forever before you. Your throne shall be established forever.” ’ ”

explanation.adult: 2 Samuel 7:16 ends with the same word twice. Read the end of each sentence.
explanation.child: Read the last word of 2 Samuel 7:16.
explanation.teen: 2 Samuel 7:16 talks about David's kingdom and throne. Look at how long each would be established.
explanation.older: 2 Samuel 7:16 closes the oracle by repeating the duration of the promise for emphasis.

teaching.extended_explanation: God's promise to David reached far beyond his own lifetime. Read 2 Samuel 7:16 again and notice the word it repeats.
teaching.takeaway: God promised that David's throne would be established forever.

prompt.adult: David asked if anyone was left of Saul's family so he could show him kindness. For whose sake did David want to do this?
prompt.child: David wanted to be kind to someone from Saul's family because of a friend. Which friend?
prompt.teen: David searched for someone from Saul's family to show kindness to. Because of whom?
prompt.older: In 2 Samuel 9:1, for whose sake did David want to show kindness?

verses.text: Now David said, “Is there still anyone who is left of the house of Saul, that I may show him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?”

explanation.adult: 2 Samuel 9:1 ends by saying for whose sake David asked. Read the last words of his question.
explanation.teen: 2 Samuel 9:1 is David's question. The last words name the person he wanted to honor.
explanation.older: 2 Samuel 9:1 shows David remembering a covenant friendship; the person is named in the final phrase (see also 9:7).

teaching.extended_explanation: David remembered a dear friend from Saul's family. Read the end of 2 Samuel 9:1 to find who.
teaching.takeaway: David showed kindness to Mephibosheth for Jonathan's sake.

prompt.adult: David wanted to build a dwelling for the LORD. Through Nathan, what did the LORD say He would make for David instead?
prompt.child: David wanted to build God a place to live. God turned it around. What did God say He would make for David?
prompt.teen: Nathan's message flipped David's plan around. What would the LORD make for David?
prompt.older: Comparing 2 Samuel 7:5 with 7:11, what did the LORD promise to make for David?

choices.text: A new city by the sea

verses.text: “Go and tell My servant David, ‘Thus says the LORD: “Would you build a house for Me to dwell in?
since the time that I commanded judges to be over My people Israel, and have caused you to rest from all your enemies. Also the LORD tells you that He will make you a house.

explanation.adult: 2 Samuel 7:5 asks whether David would build something for God. The last sentence of 2 Samuel 7:11 uses the same word for what God would do for David.
explanation.child: Read God's question in 2 Samuel 7:5. Then read the last sentence of 2 Samuel 7:11.
explanation.teen: God's question in 7:5 and His promise in 7:11 use the same word in two different ways. Find it.
explanation.older: The wordplay links 7:5 and 7:11: the word for a building in David's plan becomes a family line in God's promise (7:12-16).

teaching.extended_explanation: David planned to build for God, but God promised to build for David. Compare 2 Samuel 7:5 with the end of 7:11.
teaching.takeaway: The LORD said He would make David a house, a family line whose throne would last.
